newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Search resumes for 28 seamen in South Atlantic.
newsitem.headline: Search resumes for 28 seamen in South Atlantic.

text.p: The search resumed on Saturday for 28 seamen missing in a remote part of the South Atlantic after their ship sank while carrying sugar from Brazil to Iraq.
A South African airforce spokeswoman said a Hercules C-130 was flying to the area where the Jahan was believed to have gone down early on Friday around 680 miles west of Cape Town.
"They have extended the search area due to the uncertainty of the position on the original mayday signal," Marietta Hopley told Reuters. The Hercules took off at 9 a.m. (0700 GMT).
The plane failed to find any of the missing crew after searching for several hours on Friday.

The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in Australia picked up a mayday distress call on Thursday night saying the freighter was flooding and the crew were abandoning ship. The centre said the Jahan went down five hours afterwards.
Hopley said three ships in the area had been in radio contact with the rescue centre early on Saturday and would help in the search.
"We have to carry out a sight search. We have had no radio beacon contact nor flares. If the crew are in dinghies and the conditions stay as they are, their chances are good," she said.
There was no immediate indication what caused the sinking of the 15,022 deadweight tonne Jahan, built in 1972, registered in Belize and operated by Seatimes shipping of Singapore.
The weather in the region, midway between the South African coast and the remote island of Tristan da Cunha, was reported to be fine at the time.
A spokesman for Seatimes in Singapore said the Jahan, owned by Jahan shipping of Panama, was on charter to a London company and carrying 14,000 tonnes of sugar from Brazil to Iraq.
